auto.goal: HMO-substrate match for infant gut colonisation
auto.rationale: EVC001 expresses a dedicated H1 cluster that cleaves human milk oligosaccharides; 2'-FL is the most abundant HMO and a preferred substrate, supporting persistent colonisation.

auto.goal: Preserve probiotic viability during antibiotic course
auto.rationale: Broad-spectrum antibiotics inactivate live B. infantis; separating doses by ≥2 hours reduces direct kill and preserves colonisation, mirroring guidance for other gut probiotics.
Physiologic melatonin shortens sleep latency; glycine 3 g lowers core body temperature and improves subjective sleep quality. Mechanisms are distinct and clinically complementary.

The Ames Lab pairing combines L-carnitine (fatty-acid transport into mitochondria) with alpha-lipoic acid (PDH cofactor / Nrf2 activator). The combination improved mitochondrial function and reduced oxidative damage in aged rats and underpins several geroscience formulations.

auto.goal: Same carnitine pool — avoid double dosing
auto.rationale: ALCAR and L-carnitine share the same systemic carnitine pool; stacking both at high dose simply elevates the carnitine load. Pick one form for the indication (ALCAR for CNS effects, L-carnitine for cardiac/muscle).

auto.goal: Preserve S. boulardii viability around azole/echinocandin dosing
auto.rationale: Systemic antifungals (fluconazole, nystatin, amphotericin) are active against S. boulardii in vitro and abolish its protective effect when co-administered. Separate doses by ≥2 hours, and avoid use entirely in patients on long-term systemic antifungal therapy or with central venous catheters.

auto.goal: Acute pediatric gastroenteritis — shorten diarrhoea duration
auto.rationale: S. boulardii reduces diarrhoea duration by ~24 hours; ORS replaces ongoing fluid/electrolyte losses. ESPGHAN/ESPID guidance supports S. boulardii as an adjunct to rehydration in acute infectious diarrhoea.

auto.goal: Older-adult lean mass and strength with resistance training
auto.rationale: Creatine added to a sufficient protein intake further increases lean mass and upper-body strength in older adults performing resistance training compared with protein alone. Effect size is modest but consistent across meta-analyses.

auto.goal: Leucine metabolite overlap in older adults already meeting protein target
auto.rationale: HMB is a leucine metabolite. In patients hitting 1.2-1.5 g/kg/day high-leucine protein, additional HMB shows diminishing returns outside of disuse atrophy or critical illness. Reserve HMB for bedrest or anorexia of aging where intake is inadequate.

auto.goal: Adjunctive anxiolysis in generalised anxiety disorder
auto.rationale: Standardised chamomile extract (Matricaria recutita, 1500 mg/day) reduced GAD severity in two University of Pennsylvania RCTs; no pharmacokinetic interaction with SSRIs has been reported, and the combination is commonly used clinically.
Systemic antifungals act on S. boulardii; separate dosing by ≥2 hours and avoid in immunocompromised patients with central lines (fungaemia risk).

auto.goal: Adjunct to rehydration in acute infectious diarrhoea
auto.rationale: Meta-analysis shows S. boulardii shortens acute diarrhoea by ~1 day; ORS remains the primary intervention. The combination is widely used in pediatric care.
ESPGHAN positions LGG among the probiotics with evidence to shorten acute infectious diarrhoea by roughly one day when added to standard rehydration.
Both alkalinise urine, increase urinary citrate, and inhibit calcium oxalate crystal formation. AUA stone-prevention guidance acknowledges both as adjuncts when dietary correction is insufficient.
Many electrolyte powders already contribute 200–600 mg of potassium per serving; layering clinical-dose K-citrate on top can drive serum K out of range.

Ginger inhibits cyclo-oxygenase / thromboxane synthesis at high doses; combined chronic use with aspirin or clopidogrel could increase bruising and bleeding times. Effect size is modest at typical culinary doses.
ACOG endorses both ginger 250 mg QID and vitamin B6 (pyridoxine) 10–25 mg TID as first-line non-pharmacological options for NVP. They act via distinct mechanisms and can be combined.
Ginger inhibits COX/LOX pathways; curcumin inhibits NF-κB. Both reduce knee OA pain in meta-analyses; the combination is plausible but head-to-head trial evidence is limited.

Cribb (PMID 16766878) showed greater fat-free mass and strength gains when creatine was co-ingested with a milk protein blend than with protein alone, with casein's slow leucine release pairing well with creatine's phosphagen support.

A 30-g casein serving delivers ~200–300 mg calcium. Layering 1000 mg supplemental calcium on top of high-casein intake can exceed RDA targets and contributes to the vascular-calcification debate; pair with K2 if calcium intake is high.

Both saffron (30 mg/day) and EPA-predominant omega-3 (≥1 g EPA/day) have antidepressant signals in meta-analyses of mild-to-moderate MDD; mechanisms are distinct (serotonergic modulation vs membrane lipid composition / neuroinflammation).

Saffron 30 mg/day matched fluoxetine 40 mg/day in head-to-head trials and improved sexual-function side effects of SSRIs as adjunct. Watch for serotonin-related symptoms with high-dose serotonergic stacks.

auto.goal: Citrulline more efficiently raises plasma arginine than oral L-arginine
auto.rationale: Oral L-arginine is heavily metabolised first-pass; oral citrulline bypasses gut/liver and elevates plasma arginine more reliably. Stacking both is rarely necessary; pick citrulline if NO support is the goal.

Citrulline raises NO via the arginine/NOS pathway; beetroot raises NO via dietary nitrate / nitrite reduction. Both are ergogenic at similar magnitudes; stacking shows additive effects in some trials but with diminishing returns.
Both raise cGMP-mediated vasodilation; combining 6 g citrulline malate pre-workout with on-demand PDE5 inhibitors may potentiate dizziness, especially with concurrent antihypertensives or nitrates.

Bovine and marine collagen hydrolysates share a near-identical glycine/proline/hydroxyproline profile and comparable plasma di-/tri-peptide kinetics. Stacking both adds cost without unique benefit; pick one based on dietary preference.

auto.goal: Enhance non-heme iron absorption in women
auto.rationale: Lp299v co-ingested with a fruit-drink iron source increased non-heme iron absorption by ~50% in women of reproductive age, likely via lactic-acid lowering of luminal pH.
Like other lactic-acid bacteria, Lp299v is susceptible to most oral antibiotics; dose ≥2 hours apart and continue for the antibiotic course plus one week.
Some broad-spectrum probiotic blends already contain L. plantarum strains; check the label to avoid paying for redundant strain mass at sub-clinical CFU counts.
Lp299v showed IBS symptom relief in the Ducrotté RCT; soluble fibre provides fermentable substrate and contributes its own benefit on stool form. Combination is rational for mixed-IBS.
Both Iberogast and enteric-coated peppermint oil act as smooth-muscle relaxants for functional dyspepsia and IBS. Combining them adds cost and oesophageal-reflux risk without proven additive benefit.
Hibiscus tea lowers SBP by ~7 mmHg in meta-analysis; adding to ACE/ARB therapy may produce symptomatic hypotension or orthostasis, especially in elderly patients.
Hibiscus has mild diuretic activity; stacking with hydrochlorothiazide or loop diuretics may compound orthostatic symptoms and electrolyte shifts. Monitor BP and electrolytes during initiation.
Both lower SBP by ~5–8 mmHg via vasodilation pathways; pick one if the goal is BP and avoid layering on top of existing antihypertensive regimen without monitoring.

auto.goal: Same active constituent — hepatotoxicity dose risk
auto.rationale: Stacking a concentrated decaf EGCG product with standard green tea extract drives EGCG exposure past the EFSA 800 mg/day no-observed-adverse-effect threshold, compounding idiosyncratic hepatotoxicity risk.
EGCG and other green-tea catechins reduce non-heme iron absorption by up to 70%. In iron-deficiency anaemia, separate EGCG and iron supplements by ≥2 hours.

auto.goal: Reduces nadolol absorption via OATP1A2 inhibition
auto.rationale: Green tea catechins inhibit intestinal OATP1A2 and lower nadolol Cmax by ~85%. Separate dosing or choose a beta-blocker not dependent on OATP1A2 (e.g., bisoprolol, metoprolol).

auto.goal: Glutathione support via Nrf2 + cysteine substrate
auto.rationale: Sulforaphane activates the Nrf2/Keap1 pathway driving GSH-synthesising enzymes; NAC provides the rate-limiting cysteine. The combination raises GSH more than either alone in cell-line and small clinical studies.
Sulforaphane activates Nrf2; curcumin both activates Nrf2 and inhibits NF-κB. The pair is widely used in chemoprevention research with consistent additive effects on phase II enzyme induction.
NEM (500 mg/day) reduces joint pain and stiffness within 7–30 days in OA RCTs; glucosamine/chondroitin act on cartilage matrix metabolism over longer horizons. The pair is rational for new-onset OA.

queue_low.rationale: Saffron components (crocetin, safranal) show mild platelet-aggregation inhibition in vitro; clinical bleeding signal is theoretical. Use caution with high-dose saffron in patients on dual antiplatelet therapy.
Collagen peptides provide raw substrate for cartilage matrix; glucosamine/chondroitin modulate chondrocyte signalling pathways. Combined use is plausible but head-to-head RCT data are limited.

The original STW 5 formula included Chelidonium majus (greater celandine), which the EMA flagged for hepatotoxicity. STW 5-II has removed celandine, but some markets still sell legacy product. With chronic acetaminophen use, prefer STW 5-II or alternatives.

queue_low.goal: Nrf2 induction may alter acetaminophen metabolism
queue_low.rationale: Sulforaphane pre-treatment induces phase II enzymes and altered acetaminophen-induced hepatotoxicity in rodent models. Clinical relevance unproven; raise as caution at chronic high doses, especially with alcohol.
Both deliver collagen-type amino acids and hyaluronic-acid precursors for joint support; head-to-head trials don't show clear additivity. Pick one for OA and add the other only if symptoms persist.
NEM already contains hyaluronic acid (~1%); oral HA supplementation adds modest joint-comfort effect; combination is plausible but trial evidence is thin.

escalate.goal: Additive CNS depression and next-day sedation
escalate.rationale: Even low-dose melatonin can potentiate benzodiazepine-induced sedation, psychomotor impairment, and fall risk in older adults. Use the lowest effective dose if combined and avoid driving the following morning.

escalate.goal: Reverse valproate-induced carnitine depletion and hyperammonaemia
escalate.rationale: Valproate sequesters carnitine as valproyl-carnitine and inhibits beta-oxidation, producing secondary deficiency and hyperammonaemic encephalopathy. Pediatric Neurology Society recommends L-carnitine 100 mg/kg/day IV for symptomatic toxicity; oral supplementation is widely used for risk groups.
Chamomile contains natural coumarins and a documented INR-raising case report with intracranial bleed. Avoid concurrent chronic use; if used, monitor INR weekly until stable.

ACE inhibitors and ARBs raise serum potassium by blocking aldosterone; adding clinical-dose potassium citrate (often 30–60 mEq/day for stone or RTA management) compounds the risk, especially with reduced GFR or diabetes.
Potassium-sparing diuretics reduce renal K+ excretion; co-administration with potassium citrate produced symptomatic hyperkalaemia in case series. Avoid unless serum K+ is monitored.

escalate.goal: Possible bleeding risk via thromboxane inhibition
escalate.rationale: Case reports describe elevated INR with high-dose ginger in patients on warfarin; mechanistic data show inhibition of platelet aggregation. Avoid daily high-dose ginger (>2 g/day) without INR monitoring.

skip_dup.goal: Avoid duplicate strain in multi-strain blends
skip_dup.rationale: Many infant multi-strain blends already include B. infantis; stacking EVC001 on top adds cost without proven additive benefit unless HMO substrate is present.
Caffeine within ~6 hours of bedtime blunts the endogenous melatonin rise, partially offsetting a low physiologic dose. Separate caffeine and melatonin dosing by ≥6 hours.
Vitamin D adequacy is required for the anabolic response to protein in older adults; combined whey + leucine + D3 improved appendicular muscle mass and chair-stand performance in the PROVIDE trial.

skip_dup.goal: Separate dosing to preserve LGG viability
skip_dup.rationale: Antibiotics that are active against gram-positive flora reduce LGG counts when co-ingested. Dose LGG ≥2 hours after the antibiotic, continued ≥1 week past completion, to maximise the AAD-prevention benefit.

skip_dup.goal: 24-hour MPS coverage (already captured in p56) — pre-bed casein dosing
skip_dup.rationale: 30–40 g pre-sleep casein elevates overnight muscle protein synthesis without disturbing sleep, complementing daytime whey dosing.

Shaw et al. demonstrated that 15 g gelatin + 50 mg vitamin C taken 30–60 minutes before exercise doubled blood markers of collagen synthesis. Apply the same timing window for tendon and ligament rehabilitation protocols.
